title: SQL vs NoSQL
subtitle: Choose by access pattern: relationships want joins, and a write surge wants horizontal scale
motto: Pick the database for the questions you will ask, not the one you like
coreAddition: access-pattern split between SQL and a document store
keyInsight: A document store makes writes easy to spread but turns a join into hundreds of queries, while SQL joins well until writes outgrow one primary, so many systems keep each kind of data where it is queried.

decisions.title: Fail each side on its own workload
decisions.description: The document store fails on the feed's relationships and SQL fails on the write surge, so neither is shown as the default.
decisions.alternatives: Testing both on one workload would name a winner that flips on the other.

decisions.title: End with a split, not a verdict
decisions.description: The last frame keeps relationships in SQL and moves the write-heavy events out, and names the cost of running two stores.
decisions.alternatives: Ending on 'it depends' would leave the reader with no design to weigh.
